title: Sensei code graph — consolidated schema for visual design
purpose: One file a designer can read to see every possibility in the code graph: the containment hierarchy, every classification axis (code / docs / tests / modules / libraries), every enum value, and worked examples of each node and edge shape. Counts are from the live database so the design is grounded in the real distribution rather than an imagined one.

sourceOfTruth.storedVocabularies: database/ddl/enum/sensei/*.ddl — what is actually in the database
sourceOfTruth.producerVocabularies: crates/senseid/src/indexer/facts.rs — SymbolKind, RelationKind, RefKind, Rung, Reason
sourceOfTruth.liveCounts: Measured against the running local database on 2026-09-28, in a single repeatable-read snapshot so every figure below reconciles against every other. The database is live and indexing, so a later reading will differ slightly.

designImplications: Four million edges rules out a global force-directed layout. Every view must be SCOPED — one folder, one file, or one symbol's neighbourhood at depth N.

ONLY 40.4% OF EDGES ARE PLACED. A design that assumes a mostly-connected graph will not survive contact with the data. The unplaced majority is the normal state, not a defect backlog, and it must have a first-class visual treatment.
19.5% of nodes are test nodes. They swamp production structure when mixed in, so the test filter is a primary control, not a preference.

hierarchy.description: Containment runs through five levels. The first four are ownership and filesystem; the fifth nests inside itself.

levels.name: project
levels.meaning: A product. Owns one or more repositories.

levels.name: repository
levels.meaning: A git remote, identified by repo_key.

levels.name: folder
levels.meaning: THE INDEXING UNIT and the natural scope boundary. Self-nesting via folders.parent_id. Every node and every edge carries folder_id.
levels.note: This is the level that carries the code/docs/infra classification, via folder_role.

levels.name: file
levels.meaning: One row per tracked source file. A file is NOT a node — nodes reference it through nodes.file_id.

levels.name: node
levels.meaning: A declaration: a symbol, a doc heading, an extracted rationale. Nests further into itself via nodes.parent_id.
typicalChains: table -> column   (schema entities, spec'd not yet built)

parallelAxis.name: libraries
parallelAxis.meaning: External dependencies hang off a FOLDER, not off the containment chain. A folder reaches a library through sensei.referenced_libraries (folder_id -> library_id, version_used).
parallelAxis.note: There are two distinct external representations and they answer different questions. referenced_libraries answers 'what does this repo depend on' (1,904 libraries). Nodes named with a 'lib·' prefix answer 'which external symbol does this call reach'. A dependency panel wants the first; an edge target wants the second.

classificationAxes.description: Five independent ways to slice the graph. They are INDEPENDENT — a node can be test AND documentation AND external — so they are filters that compose, not one taxonomy.

byPurpose.warning: SPARSELY POPULATED. In the live database the overwhelming majority of folders have role NULL (12,874 of ~13,000 folder-kind rows). Design an explicit 'unclassified' state; do not assume every folder has a role.

values.meaning: A git repository root.
A workspace member / sub-package inside a repo.
Vendored content from another repository.
Tracked but not part of a repo.
An ordinary directory. The overwhelming majority.

byIndexingStatus.designImplication: A view must render a folder that is queued, indexing or failed — not just indexed ones. 'failed' and 'archived' need distinct treatments from 'not yet done'.

byContentClass.note: NOT a database column. This grouping is for presentation; the stored value is node_kind.

unclassified.warning: 7.5% of all nodes are 'unknown'. This is a large, visible population and needs a deliberate treatment rather than being filtered away silently.

byTestVsProduction.meaning: True when the node belongs to a test file, decided by path convention (tests/ dirs, *.test.*, *.spec.*, *_test.*, test_*.py, *Test.java).
byTestVsProduction.designImplication: A primary, always-visible toggle. External 'lib·' nodes are never test; reference stubs inherit the flag from their definition.

byProvenance.axis: derived from node.file_id, node.resolved and the name prefix
byProvenance.meaning: Three populations share the nodes table and a `name` column cannot tell them apart. They mean very different things about how much the graph KNOWS, and conflating them is the most common way a code-graph view misleads.

populations.name: declaration
populations.meaning: Real code that was read. Has a file and a line span.

populations.name: referenceStub
populations.predicate: file_id IS NULL AND resolved = false
populations.meaning: Referenced but never found. A known gap — show it dimmed, never drop it.

populations.name: external
populations.meaning: A third-party symbol. resolved = true, because the external symbol IS the definition. Belongs visually outside the repo boundary.

node_kind.where: STORED. sensei.nodes.kind — this is what a renderer actually reads.

values.meaning: A documentation heading. Level in props.level.
Fallback when no rule matched.
Reached like a field but backed by an accessor. Also the kind a schema INDEX will use.
Also the kind a schema TABLE / VIEW will use.
Extracted from NOTE/WHY/HACK/TODO/IMPORTANT comments. props.tag holds which.
Defined in the enum, no rows yet.
Defined in the enum, no rows yet.
Defined in the enum but parameters are carried as a typed prop on their function rather than as nodes, so this stays empty by design.

node_kind.note: 22 of 25 values have rows. The long tail (component 2, macro 2, hook 1) is real but tiny — do not design a legend that gives them equal weight to `method` at 262,331.

SymbolKind.where: PRODUCER. crates/senseid/src/indexer/facts.rs — what the Rust walk emits for a code declaration, before it is stored as a node_kind. Documented in 17-vocabulary.md §2.
SymbolKind.relationshipToNodeKind: SymbolKind covers only CODE declarations and maps onto the code subset of node_kind. The remaining node_kind values (file, package, section, rationale, doc, component, hook, extension, unknown) come from other producers — the file pass, the folder pass and the documentation indexer — not from this enum.

values.meaning: A free function.
A function owned by a type.
A type declaration.
A type declaration.
A type declaration.
A type declaration.
A type declaration.
One arm of an enum.
A name for another type. Stored as node_kind `type`.
A named value.
A named value.

Carried for reference stubs rather than declarations.

SymbolKind.reachedBy: Each kind also declares how it is REACHED — ReachedBy::Call or ReachedBy::Import — which is what lets coverage reports ask 'is this symbol reached at all?' without knowing the language.

values.meaning: A callable invokes another callable.
A use that is not a call — a type mention, a name read. Also the kind a schema FOREIGN KEY will use.
A file imports from a file or module. props.names lists the bindings.
A type provides an interface. props.relation separates a Rust trait impl from Java-style implementation.
A type extends another.

edge_kind.warning: ONLY 5 OF 11 KINDS HAVE ANY ROWS. The doc-to-code kinds (traces_to, covers, rationale_for) and the similarity kinds (duplicates, similar_to) are defined but unwritten. A design that features them prominently is designing for data that does not exist yet.

RelationKind.where: PRODUCER. Structural relations from the walk, documented in 17-vocabulary.md §3. These feed containment and the structural edge kinds rather than being stored verbatim.

values.meaning: This type owns this member. Feeds nodes.parent_id.
This module holds this declaration directly. Feeds nodes.parent_id.
Every child IS a parent (trait Sub: Super, class A extends B).
This type provides this interface.
Rust's `impl Trait for Type`, kept apart from Implements.
Included rather than inherited.
A decorator applied to a declaration.
This enum arm belongs to this enum.

RelationKind.invariant: A declaration takes EXACTLY ONE of Owns or Contains, never both: both feed nodes.parent_id, and a child with two parents has none.

RefKind.where: PRODUCER. Behavioural references from the walk.

values.meaning: Invokes the target.
Reads the target's value.
Writes the target's value.
Builds a value of the target type. Separated from Calls because factory detection needs it.
Names the target as a type — in a signature, a field, a bound. This is what makes field and parameter types edges rather than loose strings.
Invokes a macro. Distinct because what a macro expands to is not parsed, so a call inside the expansion is not a fact the walk has.
ENTERS a module. The only kind whose target is a Module.
Read from the syntax tree. Certain.
Derived from embeddings or BM25. Probable.
Drift or a gap. Uncertain.

edge_confidence.warning: EVERY edge in the live database is 'extracted'. Confidence is currently a constant, so it cannot carry visual weight today. Use resolved_via for the trust signal instead — that one actually varies.

resolved_via.where: STORED. sensei.edges.resolved_via (text). Produced from `Rung` in facts.rs; documented in 17-vocabulary.md §4.
resolved_via.deploymentStatus: NOT YET IN THE LIVE DATABASE. sensei.edges currently has 11 columns and this is not one of them. Any mock using this field is design-ahead, not live-backed.
resolved_via.description: WHY a placed edge was placed. The resolver is a LADDER: rungs are tried strongest-evidence-first and the FIRST that answers wins. The ORDER IS THE POINT — it says how far to trust this particular edge.

values.meaning: The schema itself states the relationship — a dbd SchemaModel ref. No source file was read.
values.status: PROPOSED in 20-schema-entities.md, not yet implemented. Ranked above everything because the database's own name is the identity and every other producer defers to it.

values.meaning: This file declares the target itself. Nothing is inferred.
An import in scope binds the head of the path.
This file's own text names the target — it declares the type or imports it by a package-rooted path, so it has STATED where the type lives.
A type in this scan declares the target as its member, in ANOTHER file. Rust puts an impl anywhere, so a method and its type are often apart.
A glob in scope covers the module the target sits in. The name was never written down — the weakest first-party rung.
A path rooted at this package, needing no import.
A fully spelled path outside this scan.
The language puts it in scope everywhere.

unresolved_reason.where: STORED. sensei.edges.unresolved_reason (text). Produced from `Reason` in facts.rs.
unresolved_reason.deploymentStatus: NOT YET IN THE LIVE DATABASE — same as resolved_via.
unresolved_reason.description: WHY an edge could not be placed. THIS IS NOT AN ERROR LIST. Several of these are correct, permanent outcomes and rendering them as failures teaches the reader something false. `isGap` separates the two.

values.meaning: The walk has no rule for this node kind yet. The fallback arm, so a form nobody thought about is named in the histogram instead of silently yielding nothing.
The language states no type where resolution needed one — an unannotated binding, a closure parameter. Inferring it is a non-goal.
A member access whose receiver type this file cannot determine, most often a chain deeper than the walk follows.
A bare name with no local declaration and no import binding it. NOT the same as external.
The walk minted the candidate but the shared resolution ladder has not run. The one bucket that must be EMPTY once resolution is in place — which makes it a thing a histogram can check.
More than one candidate matched and nothing distinguishes them. Picking one would be a WRONG edge, which is worse than a missing one.
The target is chosen at run time — a trait object, a function pointer. No static answer exists: a permanent miss, not a gap.
The target would only exist after macro expansion, and expansions are not parsed.
Grammar-filtered noise — clone, unwrap, toString. Filtering, not failure; its own reason so a reader can exclude it without also excluding genuine misses.

The target names a member NO first-party type declares — a method on a library type (.trim(), .collect(), .toBe()). This is where our world ends, not something we dropped. 23,739 of 53,224 receivers previously miscounted as receiver_type_unknown were actually this.
Found in a manifest.
Added deliberately for its documentation.

scan_skip_reason.where: STORED. sensei.files.skip_reason — why a file was not indexed.

declared_type_schemaObjects.where: STORED as free text in nodes.props/declared_type, but treated as a CLOSED set by convention.
declared_type_schemaObjects.description: The second level of the two-level vocabulary: the generic kind goes in node_kind so cross-language queries work, the specific word goes here.

SchemaSource.description: WHO said so. A consumer must be able to tell the schema's own word from an ORM's reading of it, because they disagree and the schema wins.

values.meaning: dbd's SchemaModel — the schema describing itself.
An ORM or data-access layer, named.

Naming.description: Whether the NAME was what the source wrote, or what a convention supplied. Load-bearing: a consumer that cannot tell them apart cannot report a mapping as verified.

values.meaning: The source wrote it — `create table sensei.orders`, an explicit `.ToTable("orders")`.
A convention supplied it — a `DbSet<Order> Orders` property, an ActiveRecord class name.

edge.verdictInvariant: Exactly one of resolved_via / unresolved_reason is set. BOTH NULL means the writer recorded no verdict — the pre-v2 shape — and is itself a category worth showing rather than hiding.

occurrences.location: props.occurrences — an object KEYED BY FILE PATH
occurrences.meaning: One edge aggregates many use sites; each entry has its own span and its own {rung, reason}. The edge-level verdict is the REDUCTION over this list.
occurrences.designImplication: An edge is not one arrow, it is a bundle. A detail panel can legitimately say 'called from 7 sites across 3 files', each with its own outcome.

renderingRules.rule: An unplaced edge is dimmed, never dropped.
renderingRules.why: The edge is real; only its endpoint is unplaceable. Dropping it makes the graph look more complete than it is — the single most misleading thing this view can do. At 59.6% unplaced, dropping them would hide most of the data.

renderingRules.rule: Split unplaced edges by isGap before styling them.
renderingRules.why: external_boundary, dynamic_dispatch, macro_expansion, plumbing and ambiguous_candidates are CORRECT outcomes. Rendering them the same as receiver_type_unknown tells the reader there is work to do where there is none.

renderingRules.rule: Scope every view; never attempt a global layout.
renderingRules.why: 4,077,549 edges. Root every view at a folder, a file or a symbol with a depth limit.

renderingRules.rule: Make the test filter a primary control.
renderingRules.why: 230,241 of 1,182,526 nodes are tests. Mixed in, they swamp production structure.

renderingRules.rule: Separate the three node populations visually.
renderingRules.why: A declaration, a reference stub and an external lib· symbol look identical if you only read `name`, but they say very different things about how much the graph knows.

renderingRules.rule: Use resolved_via rank as the trust signal, not confidence.
renderingRules.why: confidence is a constant today — every edge is 'extracted'. resolved_via is the field that actually varies, and its ladder is ordered: declared_here is a fact, through_a_glob is the weakest first-party inference.

renderingRules.rule: Design empty and unclassified states deliberately.
renderingRules.why: folder.role is NULL for most folders and 88,690 nodes are kind 'unknown'. Both are common, not edge cases. NOTE: community_id is NOT one of these — it is populated on all but 20 nodes.

renderingRules.rule: Treat an edge as a bundle of occurrences.
renderingRules.why: props.occurrences is keyed by file and each use site carries its own span and outcome, so a detail view can show where a relationship actually happens.

renderingRules.rule: A node does not have to be a circle. Nested rounded rectangles are welcome — the bar is tidy, readable, navigable.
renderingRules.why: The graph is CONTAINMENT-shaped before it is network-shaped: a file holds classes, a class holds methods, a table holds columns, and nodes.parent_id makes that nesting explicit. A circle has no natural way to show something inside it, so a force-directed ball of circles throws away the one structure the data most reliably has. A rectangle can hold its children; a label fits in it; and a nested box reads as ownership without needing an edge drawn for it. Reserve circles for the cases where nesting genuinely does not apply — an external `lib·` symbol, or a reference stub with no parent.

notYetBuilt: resolved_via and unresolved_reason are defined in the DDL but absent from the live sensei.edges table.
Schema entities (tables, columns, indexes, foreign keys as graph nodes) are specified in docs/spec/indexer/20-schema-entities.md but not implemented. All examples marked PROPOSED.
6 of 11 edge kinds have zero rows: depends_on, traces_to, covers, rationale_for, duplicates, similar_to.
edge_confidence values 'inferred' and 'ambiguous' have zero rows.

Clustering is computed but nothing reads it, and that is a DECISION rather than an oversight: issue #149 measured that 62% of communities restate the file boundary and 36% are stub singletons, so a cohesion view built on community_id would be showing the clustering algorithm rather than the architecture. Use it for grouping if it reads well; do not present it as a quality signal.
